Gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime caused by some of the most violent and energetic processes in the universe, such as the collision of black holes or neutron stars. These waves propagate at the speed of light and carry information about their origins. The detection of gravitational waves has opened up a new field of astronomy, allowing scientists to observe phenomena that are invisible to traditional telescopes [mpg](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGtIMHT5n8v9C8IDtgNh7DZffQ0332MFy9vxE-ul_vys_OqlgCBKDbu-V8peDmPdOKxSMOeUwWSBVbf97ViPIpuJ_-c_RnkJFxlNHxX5XTx_YBIq4gFR68BbDuXrw==) [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF-8WD5To6cB3LOX3sLlZy_FsmW6QIUOZEvfx_jRgOv2UmI63CRLStarRXiyeZAyP8hODCsXBA05bVX-BZiczcnUK5ObJgnox36S20URbw1zQJ3-_Z1XkaV9knFALW0UqPfgZtos3YYwESnH2oktf1ooXJFOK9-ub9kw_eQRVo3).

The primary method for detecting gravitational waves involves sophisticated instruments called laser interferometers. These observatories, such as LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory), Virgo, and KAGRA, utilize long, perpendicular arms. Lasers travel along these arms, and when a gravitational wave passes through, it minutely stretches and compresses spacetime. It's a foundational framework for scientific inquiry that has evolved over centuries, with its core principles remaining consistent while its application continues to adapt to contemporary research needs and technological advancements [apnews](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGTPIRHMWunhtk_kM7vAKXHDT01YstZbTO-MYRQjPi7AS2hw3cEqJG2nTwUdJ8EmQrzok1HaDAgWHmdwJ4DY30XLZvhwouw2DzpzlKbRCX3UTYhz6Bimojym1YmnHDOAkagJb0zUjzlyTjgh-CVd9Y-PU4W9E9twacIGdArj5WQNujuxEwgFJB_) [researchgate](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGqk6Zhwulky973F_tcqMOcpsXrI1y_0ZLKtjJ2mnNaN-3h7KE1sfwwUPcyTqFMYJELsyjBmwncm0B5H9Uom_tI89aoNaMyQ1SaK7eQYtuX7pLILjgvY5sZBArKIMPN0NHSy71sAFY8LGB-qg-aU4ievgGe4_UU7f9FWeLnGLRjIRHSN51ra0AZ76wVbg==).

The generally accepted fundamental steps of the scientific method include:

*   **Observation:** This involves noticing a phenomenon or posing a question about something observed in the natural world [sciencebuddies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGBe55MsoMX1ue5LnoO0JisX0BOI1YmHdav3lDDHfA_2N4IY6V045fdbNY2lIhSDcXkZ6cYUCCc0rNBKLM9_Tar6NlD3uxGkAaalldT3vY4np7kuneF-GRSoiAZ3BTj6_S361sqdtodlWlqM5k5kWD59pa4ddTxK0M5OmIZ1vISR1F0bEbmfcnUxk4fqjciPG7sd4EFnbtZ57dqZw==) [khanacademy](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFOb42kZobsxG07UNlDFeFGxz6fa1PbpN2SIROXoKuxHPtQb-vP0M5DJVPiyAaPUsyHRUTb32QCi4rm1uSyVDMMF5wr4BNHD_pYxQXKNqpuVTZPit6oUwyQxEqsOFRmTsHN8yiQXDRJyJtHS0mhJZg0gRPSOGaiiczYGDjMAvuJkfBRN2WC_25HLyNY0O4MKMo6XOiHlySkemEwm0Kca5T-vTLN) [globe](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFFSFzdmi8rDGv_JMbaK4GWKHbdlx5XqEbf4d-ZZTZcAF2TgGegcbE7Wk8eCBgq4PJLGkgFRTv8ugSnThJBoQyJ1Uv6wlyNyXzEc-G7DwMnE1y7Vz0j5dNRYNtqmbxiCgHWCoiu1ARBrICsxH5BfKltM1t4Ycv7GbB_J0FkB91VhL2HtgfLAtwGH3a6hS0VPzHfvET06CMjobGK1ZLRGZNxl7nMsA==).
*   **Background Research:** Before forming a hypothesis, researchers gather existing information and resources to understand what is already known about the topic [sciencebuddies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGBe55MsoMX1ue5LnoO0JisX0BOI1YmHdav3lDDHfA_2N4IY6V045fdbNY2lIhSDcXkZ6cYUCCc0rNBKLM9_Tar6NlD3uxGkAaalldT3vY4np7kuneF-GRSoiAZ3BTj6_S361sqdtodlWlqM5k5kWD59pa4ddTxK0M5OmIZ1vISR1F0bEbmfcnUxk4fqjciPG7sd4EFnbtZ57dqZw==) [thoughtco](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDyZKegrc1S0B6m6_J1FhCRL3m4EuPlfmmX112RalcaJZ9bgGpiwrH5KrmICRycH-dDDyg2dtyU16RGhfCNdk6qniQQP7v_2kTUI_Rb_ld0J20VzJnMsdSKTT7edukA6TD0pHcJARw-IfSmcYkovNJkoSRodkx6RMNadQFXQ==).
*   **Hypothesis Formation:** This is the development of a testable explanation or an educated guess to answer the initial question. A hypothesis should lead to a prediction that can be tested [sciencebuddies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGBe55MsoMX1ue5LnoO0JisX0BOI1YmHdav3lDDHfA_2N4IY6V045fdbNY2lIhSDcXkZ6cYUCCc0rNBKLM9_Tar6NlD3uxGkAaalldT3vY4np7kuneF-GRSoiAZ3BTj6_S361sqdtodlWlqM5k5kWD59pa4ddTxK0M5OmIZ1vISR1F0bEbmfcnUxk4fqjciPG7sd4EFnbtZ57dqZw==) [khanacademy](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFOb42kZobsxG07UNlDFeFGxz6fa1PbpN2SIROXoKuxHPtQb-vP0M5DJVPiyAaPUsyHRUTb32QCi4rm1uSyVDMMF5wr4BNHD_pYxQXKNqpuVTZPit6oUwyQxEqsOFRmTsHN8yiQXDRJyJtHS0mhJZg0gRPSOGaiiczYGDjMAvuJkfBRN2WC_25HLyNY0O4MKMo6XOiHlySkemEwm0Kca5T-vTLN) [thoughtco](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDyZKegrc1S0B6m6_J1FhCRL3m4EuPlfmmX112RalcaJZ9bgGpiwrH5KrmICRycH-dDDyg2dtyU16RGhfCNdk6qniQQP7v_2kTUI_Rb_ld0J20VzJnMsdSKTT7edukA6TD0pHcJARw-IfSmcYkovNJkoSRodkx6RMNadQFXQ==).
*   **Experimentation:** Researchers design and conduct experiments to test their hypothesis. A key aspect of experimentation is changing only one variable at a time to ensure a fair test. Repeating experiments is also important for reliability [sciencebuddies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGBe55MsoMX1ue5LnoO0JisX0BOI1YmHdav3lDDHfA_2N4IY6V045fdbNY2lIhSDcXkZ6cYUCCc0rNBKLM9_Tar6NlD3uxGkAaalldT3vY4np7kuneF-GRSoiAZ3BTj6_S361sqdtodlWlqM5k5kWD59pa4ddTxK0M5OmIZ1vISR1F0bEbmfcnUxk4fqjciPG7sd4EFnbtZ57dqZw==) [thoughtco](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDyZKegrc1S0B6m6_J1FhCRL3m4EuPlfmmX112RalcaJZ9bgGpiwrH5KrmICRycH-dDDyg2dtyU16RGhfCNdk6qniQQP7v_2kTUI_Rb_ld0J20VzJnMsdSKTT7edukA6TD0pHcJARw-IfSmcYkovNJkoSRodkx6RMNadQFXQ==).
*   **Data Analysis:** After the experiment, data is collected and analyzed to determine whether it supports or refutes the hypothesis [sciencebuddies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGBe55MsoMX1ue5LnoO0JisX0BOI1YmHdav3lDDHfA_2N4IY6V045fdbNY2lIhSDcXkZ6cYUCCc0rNBKLM9_Tar6NlD3uxGkAaalldT3vY4np7kuneF-GRSoiAZ3BTj6_S361sqdtodlWlqM5k5kWD59pa4ddTxK0M5OmIZ1vISR1F0bEbmfcnUxk4fqjciPG7sd4EFnbtZ57dqZw==) [thoughtco](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHDyZKegrc1S0B6m6_J1FhCRL3m4EuPlfmmX112RalcaJZ9bgGpiwrH5KrmICRycH-dDDyg2dtyU16RGhfCNdk6qniQQP7v_2kTUI_Rb_ld0J20VzJnMsdSKTT7edukA6TD0pHcJARw-IfSmcYkovNJkoSRodkx6RMNadQFXQ==).
*   **Conclusion:** Based on the data analysis, conclusions are drawn. Key greenhouse gases responsible for trapping heat include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O). CO2 is the largest contributor, accounting for approximately 42% of the increase in global surface temperatures since the pre-industrial era, followed by methane at about 28% and nitrous oxide at around 5% [carbonbrief](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=0).

In 2025, greenhouse gas concentrations reached new highs, driven by human-caused emissions from fossil fuels, land use, and agriculture [carbonbrief](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=0). Global fossil CO2 emissions were projected to rise by 1.1% in 2025, reaching a record high of approximately 38.1 billion metric tons, attributed to the growth in global energy demand that is not being fully offset by the decarbonization of energy systems [globalcarbonbudget](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=1) [lmu](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=2). Emissions from all fossil fuel sources—coal, oil, and natural gas—were expected to increase globally in 2025 [lmu](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=2).

While human-caused greenhouse gas emissions are the underlying cause of long-term global warming, short-term fluctuations in global mean temperature are primarily driven by internal variations within the climate system, such as the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon [berkeleyearth](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=3) [carbonbrief](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG3GHz98s8KNZRyxVSxftNWsoNCxvwI4EL-ZqS8y2fVKRAVbAS9CD6u0JOGNR4FqIZTIHrZEB0nRfJk_Q2ZidkXgOC1oskktV_I8nfrQDod0QbEicErX_n0Yvgl0ZPSIW_4DIE=0) [downtoearth](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFLBLgEjpTTjy5J5pL_wtu384JdWPDLpj7qKnM2aHPqGaW-jlQ5dmMW39MXLeQFekJ-ggkqKvSyGjF9eP74WBTra6nAqT2RwljwmyQpvdvR9IgkPXsSzZplEoymhpIMhtAroer6W-ajX99PsNw9h9H4W3JlnTixovLsa-4q1IIC0WlliR7XEk_WAhZ24hBPihFRI3Od1QQIGDoJ24ehjaOe4YMU-6idrnE0x36M24c5VKw_6e8DsMqPVUM=).
